purpose: Country evidence register entry. This record documents sourced agricultural context and identifies data suitable for later validation; it is not an enterprise budget, price feed, or calculator profile.

evidence.topic: 2026 cereal production outlook and import requirement

values.note: FAO forecast; about 20 percent below the five-year average.
About 7 percent above average; includes cereals, not a domestic farm output measure.
More than 40 percent of total cereal imports; about 12 percent above average.
FAO reports approximately 18 percent year-on-year food inflation.
FAO reports the dinar weakened by about 15 percent year-on-year; this is a macroeconomic context indicator, not an input-price conversion.

caveats: 2026 crop production is a forecast, not final post-harvest statistics.
FAO notes delayed planting after dry weather in October-November 2025 and below-average precipitation in eastern producing areas, particularly Al Jabal Al Akhdar.
Do not use national cereal balance/import figures as farm-level yield, revenue, or profitability inputs.

evidence.source: World Bank World Development Indicators (FAOSTAT-sourced cereal production) and SESRIC Libya in Figures

values.note: World Bank WDI identifies FAO as source and reports 164,800 tonnes.
SESRIC country profile, drawing on international agricultural statistics.
Equivalent to approximately 0.6597 tonnes per hectare; retain source unit for traceability.
Equivalent to approximately 0.0513 tonnes per hectare as displayed by SESRIC; unusually low relative to the reported barley production/area ratio and therefore requires validation before use.

caveats: The cereal aggregate production value is supported by the World Bank WDI page citing FAO; area and yield are taken from SESRIC and should be cross-checked against the underlying FAOSTAT download.
The barley yield displayed by SESRIC appears inconsistent with the ratio of 65,000 tonnes divided by 126,698 hectares. Do not silently correct it; flag for source-level reconciliation.
These are national statistical series, not farm-specific performance benchmarks.

evidence.source: Natlas country agriculture data compilation citing FAOSTAT 2024
caveats: This is a secondary compilation, not the primary FAOSTAT interface. Figures are discovery leads and must be checked against the exact FAOSTAT item/element/year before operational use.
Livestock inventory and annual production of meat, milk, or eggs are different measures; do not treat them as interchangeable.
These aggregate production values do not establish district-specific yields, farm-gate prices, or net margins.

evidence.topic: Monthly food price estimates by product and market
evidence.source: World Bank Microdata Library, Real-Time Food Prices, Libya version 2026-10-05

values.unit: listed product/price series including duplicates and index/exchange series
values.note: Includes beans, bread, chickpeas, chili, eggs, chicken, lamb, milk, oil, onions, pasta, potatoes, rice, tomatoes, wheat flour and other food items.

evidence.methodology: World Bank DECDG Real-Time Prices combines direct price measurements from WFP, FAO and selected national statistical offices with machine-learning imputation for missing observations. The dataset includes modeled Open/High/Low/Close estimates and may adjust outliers.
caveats: These are consumer/market food price estimates, not farm-gate producer prices.
The series include imputed/modelled observations; use the dataset's coverage and imputation diagnostics and distinguish observed from estimated values.
The price data are useful for market context and retail/food inflation analysis but must not be used as crop selling prices or farm revenue without independent farm-gate validation.
No individual LYD price values have been transcribed into this register because the downloadable microdata were not extracted in this research pass.

evidence.source: Libya Trade Network, Libyan Ministry of Economy and Trade open-data platform

values.value: annual highs, lows, averages and percentage change
food, meat, poultry, eggs, vegetables, fruits, grains and animal feed

caveats: The source describes local market prices, not necessarily farm-gate producer prices.
The XLSX resource is published, but its contents were not extracted in this pass; no numerical price claims are made.
Before calculator use, inspect commodity definitions, unit, market location, date, tax/transport treatment and whether prices are wholesale or retail.

evidence.topic: Farm structure, crop geography and livestock systems
evidence.source: IFAD, The State of Libya: Country Strategy Note 2023-2024

values.note: IFAD reports approximately 20 percent of rural households engaged in agriculture.

crop_and_region_notes: Tomatoes, peppers, onions and leafy greens are commonly grown.
Olives and pulses are important in Al Jabal Al Gharbi; citrus in Derna; dates in Al Jufra.
Barley and fodder are notable in Fezzan in association with livestock systems.
Sheep are the most common small ruminant, followed by goats; many livestock-keeping households own fewer than ten small ruminants.
Poultry keeping is noted in Wadi Ashshati and Sebha; larger-scale production is more common in coastal areas such as Benghazi.
caveats: The country strategy is dated 2022 and contains historical or secondary estimates; it is not a current agricultural census.
IFAD explicitly notes the lack of detailed, reliable and recent agricultural-sector data in the background study.
Area estimates cited from Aquastat are for 2016 and must not be presented as current land-use statistics.

evidence.source: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, World Food Programme and Tatweer Research, Fezzan Agricultural Assessment executive summary

values.value: Fezzan region, including productive-unit and farmer profiles
first assessment of smallholder farmers since 2006

caveats: The WFP publication page confirms the assessment and its institutional authorship; detailed numeric tables from the full report have not been extracted in this pass.
Regional Fezzan findings must not be generalized to all Libya without a national sampling frame.

evidence.source: FAO, Integrated methodological framework and assessment of water management infrastructure, crop and water productivity in Libya

values.note: FAO describes satellite imagery and more than 750 field surveys.

caveats: The study identified critical damage to irrigation infrastructure and recommends repairs, system upgrades, monitoring and training.
The landing page does not provide crop-by-crop irrigation costs or water productivity numeric tables; these must be extracted from the linked full report before modelling.

evidence.topic: Agricultural statistical system and census preparation
evidence.source: Libya Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, agricultural census programme update

values.value: WCA 2030 preparatory training completed; full agricultural census preparation underway

caveats: The Ministry describes capacity-building and preparation for a comprehensive agricultural census, not publication of completed census results.
This supports the assessment that a current, complete national farm census dataset was not located in this research pass.

strengths: Current FAO GIEWS 2026 cereal outlook and import balance.
A World Bank 41-market monthly food-price dataset updated through 2026-10-01.
An official Libya Trade Network local market price dataset for 2024-2025.
FAOSTAT-sourced national crop and livestock leads for 2024.
IFAD regional farm-structure context, WFP/Ministry smallholder assessment, and FAO irrigation-infrastructure research.
material_gaps: No verified current farm-gate producer price series extracted.
No validated crop-specific enterprise budgets for seed, fertilizer, crop protection, labour, irrigation energy, machinery, land rent, packaging and transport.
Official 2024-2025 local market-price workbook contents have not been extracted or classified by wholesale/retail level.
World Bank Real-Time Food Price estimates are consumer-market series with imputation and are not farm-gate prices.
The 2024 crop and livestock totals need direct FAOSTAT item/element verification; barley yield metadata has an apparent internal inconsistency.
No completed current agricultural census tables were located; the Ministry reported census preparation in January 2026.
Irrigation-water costs and groundwater sustainability vary by region and are not represented by a single national cost.
conditions_before_calculator_activation: Extract and independently validate FAOSTAT crop area, production and yield series by item and year.
Download and inspect the official 2024-2025 local market-price workbook; classify each commodity price as farm-gate, wholesale or retail and retain location, date and unit.
Extract the World Bank monthly price microdata only for market context, retaining observed/imputed flags and market coverage.
Obtain current region-specific farm-gate prices and supplier quotations for inputs.
Build crop-specific enterprise budgets with explicit irrigation, fuel/electricity, labour and logistics assumptions.
Validate all units, currency, exchange-rate basis and reference dates with local agricultural institutions or extension partners.
